subject: Renewal + expansion: proposed commit reshuffle, retention credits, and invoice cadence
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@team.sparrow.ai>, procurement@sparrow.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-01-20T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal + expansion: proposed commit reshuffle, retention credits, and invoice cadence

Hi Alyssa / Sparrow procurement team,

Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. Per our roadmap review, Sparrow will be 2x-ing downstream inference volume over the next 12 months and wants predictable economics while avoiding a long-term step-change in committed spend. Attached is a first-pass renewal proposal that tries to balance those priorities:

- 12-month renewal with a flexible commit reshuffle: move 30% of Year 1 committed tokens into a burst pool earmarked for Q2–Q4 spiking usage (no excess overage for bursts up to the pool).
- Retention credit: one-time credit equal to 10% of current annual spend applied as invoice credit across the first 3 invoices to smooth cashflow.
- Price hold: freeze unit price for 6 months after renewal effective date; thereafter standard quarterly indexing applies.
- Invoice cadence: option to move to Net30 or a Net45 with a one-time invoice timing credit to offset timing delta.

Two asks from our side: a firm expected 12-month consumption baseline to size the burst pool and confirmation that Sparrow procurement can sign the attached term sheet and route legal redlines to Marco.

If this looks directionally right, I propose a short working session next Wednesday to lock the MA P (mutual action plan), followed by a single redline pass.

Mina
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Sparrow_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf (pdf, 72KB)

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@team.sparrow.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sparrow.ai>, procurement@sparrow.ai
Date: 2028-01-24T10:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion: proposed commit reshuffle, retention credits, and invoice cadence

Mina — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear proposal. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Capacity: the 2x number is accurate but it ramps — Q2 is +50%, Q3 +150%, Q4 +200%. We need the burst pool to be flexible across quarters rather than Q2–Q4 locked. Can you confirm whether the burst pool can be drawn down in Q2 and refilled for Q4?

2) Credits: the retention credit is appreciated. Can that be applied as a line-item credit rather than spread across invoices? Our finance ops prefers a single credit line in the first invoice for reconciliation.

3) Invoice cadence: Net45 would help our cash cycle this year. If Redwood can provide an invoice timing credit, we should be able to agree to the Net45; please indicate the amount you had in mind.

4) Legal: Marco will lead redlines; he asked whether you have SOC 2 type II evidence and an export/control appendix we can reference.

Can we do a 30-minute alignment on Thursday 1/26 9:30am PT?

—Alyssa
Head of Procurement, Sparrow AI

Forwarded as requested: procurement@sparrow.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@team.sparrow.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-10T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion: proposed commit reshuffle, retention credits, and invoice cadence

Alyssa — appreciate the specifics. I ran the numbers with Finance and Product; here's a revised, operationally actionable counterproposal:

- Flexible burst pool: we'll size an annual burst pool equal to 35% of Year 1 committed tokens. The pool can be partitioned across quarters on demand (you can draw down and we will top-up via mutual-notice up to the pool ceiling once per quarter). This preserves predictability while allowing the ramp you described.
- Retention credit: we can convert the 10% retention credit into a single line-item credit on the first invoice (applies immediately to the invoice following renewal execution).
- Invoice timing credit: to enable Net45 we propose a one-time invoice timing credit equal to 5% of the first quarter invoice (applied as a credit).
- Price hold: six-month unit price freeze stands. After six months we will apply a modest quarterly CPI-indexed adjustment (not to exceed 1.75%/quarter).

Attached is a revised term sheet (Sparrow_TermSheet_Revised_20280210.docx) showing the above and the operational definitions for "burst pool draw" and "top-up notice." We also added an SLA carveout describing excess-use mediation to avoid unilateral overage disputes.

If these terms work, we can prepare a DocuSign packet next week. Our proposed deal id is DL-7839.

Ben Carter
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Sparrow_TermSheet_Revised_20280210.docx (docx, 48KB)

From: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sparrow.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@team.sparrow.ai>, procurement@sparrow.ai
Date: 2028-02-15T08:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion: proposed commit reshuffle, retention credits, and invoice cadence

Ben / Mina — thanks for the revised sheet. A few legal redlines from our side (high level):

- SLA: we need a more prescriptive data-retention and audit-log window for the private deployment data path; propose 12 months retention guarantee and monthly audit logs within 72 hours of request.
- SOC2: please attach the latest SOC 2 Type II report and the applicable scope. Marco also asked for the KMS/HSM controls summary for the private option.
- DocuSign flow: we prefer countersign on the same packet. Can Redwood produce a single packet with term sheet + an export/control appendix + the invoice credit schedule so we can countersign in one pass?

Minor commercial ask: can the Net45 invoice timing credit be a fixed dollar amount rather than a percent? Procurement prefers fixed amounts for POing. If Redwood proposes a fixed credit, please put it in the sheet.

I'll circulate a redline by EOD Friday.

—Marco Ruiz
Senior Counsel, Sparrow AI

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marco Ruiz <marco.ruiz@sparrow.ai>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@team.sparrow.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-02-20T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + expansion: proposed commit reshuffle, retention credits, and invoice cadence

Marco / Alyssa — appreciate the thoughtful redlines. Next steps from Redwood:

1) We will upload the SOC 2 Type II scope and the KMS/HSM controls summary to the Drive folder (link below) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Finance confirms we can convert the Net45 timing credit to a fixed $12,500 credit on the first invoice (Ben to reflect this in the next term sheet version).
3) We'll prepare a single DocuSign packet containing: revised term sheet, export/control appendix, invoice-credit schedule, and the mutual action plan. Goal: one countersign pass.

Proposed mutual action plan and timing:
- 2028-02-22: Redwood shares updated term sheet with fixed-credit number and SOC2 artifacts.
- 2028-02-24: 30-min legal alignment (Marco + Redwood legal + Ben).
- 2028-02-28: DocuSign packet sent for signature.
- 2028-03-05: Anticipated effective date (if countersigned on time).

Can Alyssa confirm the 30-minute slot on 2/24 at 11:00am PT? If yes, I'll lock the calendar and route the packet next week.

Thanks,
Mina
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Related links: https://drive.company.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-sparrow-renewal (SOC2 & controls), https://hubspot.company.com/deals/DL-7839
